answer: Make every grading seat expensive to reuse by binding it to a dated stake that decays with each verdict an operator casts. A farm that rotates identities through the same karst-cut infrastructure still needs fresh stake per seat, and the ferrous collateral locked against each one cannot be pooled across wallets without visible on-ledger trails. Like fruit in an orchard, reputation ripens only where a single agent keeps showing up honestly over many epochs.
